question.problem:
Write $\frac{8{x}^{2}}{4x-5}$ in the form $ax+\frac{bx}{4x-5},$ where $a\ne 0.$
$8{x}^{2}$ $=$ {{field-1}} $x\,+\,$ {{field-2}}
$4x-5$ $4x-5$
question.worked_solution:
First, we factor the numerator to put $4x$ in parentheses. Then, we subtract and add $5$ in the parentheses. This reveals a copy of the denominator without changing the value of the expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8{x}^{2}}{4x-5} & =\frac{2x(4x)}{4x-5} \\  & =\frac{2x(4x-5+5)}{4x-5} \\  & =\frac{2x[(4x-5)+(5)]}{4x-5} \\  & =\frac{2x(4x-5)+2x(5)}{4x-5} \\  & =\frac{2x(4x-5)+10x}{4x-5}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we split the fraction into two, and then simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x(4x-5)+10x}{4x-5} & =\frac{2x(4x-5)}{4x-5}+\frac{10x}{4x-5} \\  & =2x+\frac{10x}{4x-5}\end{aligned}
$$
